records.source: 'Nit sag̲ootxwhl government siwetdiit, ii dim 'nii wenhl dim jok̲hl aluugigyet g̲o'ohl lax̲ reserve siwetdiit.
records.reference: The plan of the so-called government was that they will have Indian people live on a so-called reserve.
records.original_response:
The Gitksan government is not, it is not the same as the government of the reserve.

(Note: The sentence structure and phrasing suggest a contrast or negation — “Nit sag̲ootxwhl government siwetdiit” = “The Gitksan government is not,” and “ii dim 'nii wenhl dim jok̲hl aluugigyet g̲o'ohl lax̲ reserve siwetdiit” = “it is not the same as the government of the reserve.” The repetition of “ii dim 'nii” may be a stylistic or emphatic construction, possibly meaning “it is not” or “it is not the same.” The translation preserves the contrastive meaning while rendering it naturally in English.)

Alternatively, a more literal but still natural rendering:

“The Gitksan government is not — it is not the same as the reserve’s government.”

But given the context and the likely intent to emphasize distinction, the first version is more idiomatic.

✅ Final translation:  
**The Gitksan government is not, it is not the same as the government of the reserve.**
